prompt: Turn brief.md into the final browser presentation. The purpose, length, content, density, outline, and visual direction are already approved in the brief, so proceed directly to the finished deck without asking questions or generating previews. Create deck/index.html and any local CSS or JavaScript it needs. The deck must be self-contained, have exactly 7 slides, work with keyboard navigation, include a visible progress indicator, use the approved visual direction rather than a generic bullet template, and use a fixed 1920x1080 stage that scales to the viewport without slide scrolling. Do not use remote images or libraries. Include speaker notes in deck/notes.md and a print stylesheet for PDF export.
setup: mkdir -p deck && printf '%s\n' '# Relay' 'An AI incident-response copilot for small engineering teams.' '' 'Purpose: seed pitch. Audience: seed investors. Length: exactly 7 slides. Density: low-density, speaker-led.' 'Approved outline: title; pain; product; workflow; traction; business model; raise.' 'Approved visual direction: calm Swiss technical editorial, off-white paper, charcoal type, safety-orange signal marks, precise grid, restrained timeline diagrams.' 'Facts: private beta; 12 design partners; no revenue yet; $1.2M seed raise; setup under 15 minutes; Slack and GitHub only.' 'Tone: technical, calm, credible. Avoid invented metrics.' > brief.md
rubric: The presentation is an authored seven-slide narrative, visually coherent and readable at the requested canvas, faithful to every supplied fact, free of invented traction, keyboard-operable, self-contained, and ready for browser presentation or PDF export.

source_failure.signature: generic bullet-heavy AI decks ignore narrative visual direction and export readiness
